General practitioners (GPs) should consider using patients' first names more often, particularly with younger patients. This approach can help build trust and improve communication with patients. While some older patients may prefer formal titles, many younger patients appreciate the personal touch and can benefit from a more conversational approach.

It's essential to note that GPs have varying levels of comfort and familiarity with using first names in their patient interactions, depending on factors such as patient age and individual preferences. However, research suggests that GP-patient relationships built on trust and rapport are crucial for effective communication and care.

In summary, while there may not be a one-size-fits-all answer to this question, using patients' first names can be a valuable strategy for improving healthcare communication and outcomes, particularly with younger patients who tend to prefer more personalized interactions.
